title: Interfacing Microfluidics with Microelectrode Arrays for Studying Neuronal Communication and Axonal Signal Propagation
protocol: Prepare 10 mL of a 0.05% (v/v) Poly(ethylene imine) (PEI) working solution.
Dissolve purified PEI in sterile water to prepare 20 mL of a 0.25% (w/v) PEI stock solution.
Dilute 2 mL of the 0.25% (w/v) PEI stock solution in 8 mL of sterile distilled water.
Mix well and use, store unused solution at 4°C.
Prepare 1 mL of a 5 µg/mL laminin solution by diluting 5 µL of a 1 mg/mL laminin stock solution in 995 µL of basal medium.
Mix well and use, store unused solution frozen at -20°C for up to 1-2 weeks.
Prepare 1 M HEPES solution by dissolving 11.9 g of HEPES powder in 50 mL of ultrapure water.
Adjust pH to 7.2.
Dissolve 5.33 mM potassium chloride, 0.44 mM potassium phosphate monobasic, 138 mM sodium chloride, 0.3 mM sodium phosphate dibasic and 5.6 mM glucose in 800 mL of ultrapure water.
Add 15 mL of 1 M HEPES solution to the mixture.
Adjust pH to 0.2-0.3 units below pH 7.4 using 1 N HCl or 1 N NaOH.
Add ultrapure water to make up the final volume for H-HBSS.
Sterilize the H-HBSS by filtration through a 0.22 μm PES membrane.
Prepare 10 mL of H-HBSS containing 10% heat-inactivated Fetal Bovine Serum (hiFBS).
Dissolve 7.5 mg of trypsin in 5 mL of H-HBSS immediately before use.
Sterilize the trypsin solution by filtration through a 0.22 μm PES membrane.
Mix 48.5 mL of basal medium with 2% B-27 supplement, 0.5 mM L-glutamine and 1% Pen/Strep in a 50 mL conical tube to prepare supplemented medium.
Store the supplemented medium at 4 °C for up to 3-4 weeks.
Clean microfluidic devices using vinyl tape to remove fabrication debris.
Air plasma-clean the MEA for 3 minutes at 0.3 mbar.
Submerge microfluidic devices in 70% ethanol and allow them to air-dry inside a laminar flow hood.
Place each MEA in a sterile 90 mm Petri dish.
Sterilize MEAs by exposing them to ultraviolet light for 15 minutes.
Incubate the MEA central surface area with 500 µL of 0.05% (v/v) PEI solution for at least 1 hour at 37 °C.
Aspirate the PEI coating solution from the MEA surface.
Wash MEAs four times with 1 mL of sterile distilled water without touching the surface.
Center the MEA chip under a stereomicroscope in a laminar flow hood.
Add 1 mL of sterile water to the central area of MEA.
Place the microfluidic device on top of the MEA surface.
Carefully align the microgrooves of the microfluidic device with the microelectrode grid of the MEA.
Aspirate excess water without touching the MEA or the microfluidic device.
Incubate µEFs overnight at 37 °C to allow complete attachment.
Gently press the microfluidic device against the MEA to facilitate attachment.
Disinfect the working surface and surgical instruments with 70% ethanol.
Use a clean disposable diaper to confine the dissection area.
Lay out surgical instruments for embryo removal.
Prepare four 90 mm Petri dishes filled with cold H-HBSS and place them on an ice tray near the dissection area.
Euthanize an E-18 time-pregnant Wistar rat by CO2 inhalation.
Confirm death by a secondary method such as exsanguination.
Place the animal ventral side up on the disposable diaper.
Spray the lower abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Make a U-shape cut through the skin to expose the uterus using forceps and scissors.
Carefully remove embryos from the uterus and place them in one of the Petri dishes filled with cold H-HBSS.
Remove each embryo from its embryonic sac.
Decapitate the embryo using forceps and scissors.
Transfer the embryo's head to a second Petri dish filled with cold H-HBSS.
Dissect the prefrontal cortex.
Transfer an embryo’s head to a third Petri dish.
Expose the brain using a pair of forceps.
Remove the brain from its cavity and cover it with cold H-HBSS.
If present, remove and discard the olfactory bulbs.
Dissect the prefrontal cortex and remove meninges.
Transfer the prefrontal cortex fragments to a fourth Petri dish filled with cold H-HBSS.
Discard the supernatant containing trypsin.
Add 5 mL of H-HBSS with 10% hiFBS to inactivate remaining trypsin; gently agitate.
Discard the supernatant after fragments settle down.
Add 5 mL of H-HBSS and discard the supernatant after fragments settle down.
Wash cortex fragments again with 5 mL of H-HBSS and discard the supernatant.
Add 5 mL of supplemented neuronal medium to cortex fragments.
Mechanically dissociate cortex fragments using a 5 mL serologic pipette for 10-15 times.
If necessary, repeat mechanical dissociation using a small caliber pipette until homogenous suspension is achieved.
Discard undissociated tissues by filtering cell suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer.
Add 20 µL of 0.4% (w/v) Trypan Blue to a 20 µL cell suspension and mix well.
Transfer 10 µL of the mixture to a Neubauer counting chamber.
Count viable cells to determine cell density.
Adjust cell density to 3.6 x 10^7 cells/mL as needed, centrifuging if necessary.
Pipette 50 µL of supplemented medium into each well of the µEF axonal compartment immediately before seeding.
Seed 5 μL of cell suspension in the µEF somal compartment.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h to allow cells attachment to the substrate.
Gently fill each well of µEF with warmed supplemented medium.
Transfer the µEF to a humidifier incubator at 37 °C supplied with 5% CO2.
Replace 50% of culture medium every second to third day of culture.
Immerse the µEF in water overnight to detach microfluidics from MEAs after experiments if needed.
Gently peel the microfluidics using forceps if necessary.
Clean MEAs by overnight incubation with a 1% (v/v) commercial enzymatic detergent.
Turn on the MEA recording system and the temperature controller.
Allow the heated base plate of the preamplifier to reach 37 °C.
Place the µEF on the preamplifier (headstage).
Ensure that the MEA chip is correctly aligned with the reference number in the upper left edge.
Close and latch the preamplifier lid.
Open the recording software.
Define the recording parameters and the path of the recorded data streams.
Set a sampling rate of 20 kHz for most applications.
Use a higher sampling frequency if more precision in spike timings is required.
Set a high-pass filter at 300 Hz to attenuate lower frequency components of the signal.
Limit microelectrodes from which to record to reduce data file size.
Click Start DAQ to start data acquisition.
Check if the display shows running traces of activity and start recording.
If peak-to-peak amplitude is >50 µV or unsteady in several microelectrodes, clean MEA contact pads and preamplifier pins using a cotton swab moistened with 70% ethanol.
Open recorded file in analysis software to explore data.
Load data into µSpikeHunter software.
Identify propagating spike waves using µSpikeHunter software.
Determine direction of spike wave propagation (anterograde or retrograde) using µSpikeHunter software.
Estimate propagation velocities using µSpikeHunter software.
Click Browse to select the recording file.
Click File Info to list sampling rate, recording duration, and recorded data streams.
Select microelectrodes for analysis.
Set spike detection threshold value at 6x the standard deviation of signal noise.
Click Read Data to apply event detector and obtain identified propagation sequences.
Save All Events to save time and amplitude of spikes for all identified propagation sequences to a CSV file.
Import CSV files to data analysis environments for further analysis.
